keyVerseText: And he took their king's crown from off his head, the weight whereof was a talent of gold with the precious stones: and it was set on David's head. And he brought forth the spoil of the city in great abundance. in great: Heb. very great
rootMeaning: The Hebrew root עָטַר (ʻâṭar) fundamentally conveys the idea of encircling or surrounding, often with the purpose of attack or protection. From this root, the noun עֲטָרָה (ʻăṭârâh) emerges, signifying a crown or wreath—an object that literally encircles the head. This root sense of surrounding enriches the English concept of a crown by emphasizing not just its ornamental value but its encompassing and protective symbolism, suggesting authority and honor that surrounds and upholds the wearer.
usageInScripture: The term עֲטָרָה appears 23 times in the Hebrew Bible, consistently translated as 'crown' or 'the crown,' reflecting its primary meaning as a royal or symbolic headpiece. It is used to describe literal crowns of gold and precious stones, such as the king's crown taken in 2 Samuel 12:30, as well as figurative crowns representing honor and splendor, for example in Jeremiah and Ezekiel. The word also appears in plural forms, indicating multiple crowns or wreaths, and is applied in diverse contexts including idol images and personified Jerusalem, revealing a rich semantic range tied to glory, dignity, and divine favor.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עֲטָרָה as a crown rooted in the concept of encircling authority deepens our appreciation of biblical imagery portraying God’s sovereign rule and the honor bestowed upon His people. The crown symbolizes not only earthly kingship but also the spiritual honor and glory that God grants to those who walk faithfully before Him. In the Christian faith, this word points forward to the ultimate crown given by Christ—the reward of righteousness and eternal life. Recognizing the crown as both a physical and figurative emblem reminds believers of the call to live under God’s protection and to bear the dignity of His kingdom.
keyVerseReflection: In 2 Samuel 12:30, the crown taken from the enemy king and placed on David’s head vividly illustrates the transfer of authority and divine approval. The description of the crown’s weight and precious stones emphasizes its value and honor. Here, עֲטָרָה signifies more than a mere ornament; it represents the tangible symbol of kingship and victory. This use reinforces the idea that the crown is a visible sign of God’s sovereign blessing and the legitimacy of David’s reign.
